page: Amazon Web Services r6id.16xlarge is a memory-optimized instance running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It is powered by a dedicated 32-core, 64-thread Intel Xeon 8375C processor operating at 3.5 GHz on the x86_64 platform. The system is configured with 512 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, establishing an 8 GB per vCPU allocation ratio. Storage includes 3800 GB of directly attached local NVMe SSD instance storage, paired with a baseline network bandwidth of 25 Gbps. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512 with VNNI, AES-NI, VAES, and Intel Total Memory Encryption.

Benchmark evaluations position this instance in the top quartile for compute-heavy and data-centric workloads. It achieves strong results in PassMark database operations, PassMark overall CPU computation, cryptographic testing, and software compilation via clang. Synthetic multi-core execution through stress-ng and Geekbench aligns within median performance tiers. Memory performance registers uncached large-block read speeds of 166.18 GB/sec and write speeds of 67.32 GB/sec, alongside a throughput of 55.35 million operations per second during Redis SET benchmarks.

The integration of dense DDR4 system memory with 3800 GB of local NVMe storage reduces latency for high-throughput transactional and analytical workloads, mitigating external storage throughput bottlenecks. While the platform lacks dedicated GPU acceleration, it maintains stable throughput for CPU-based inference on smaller parameter models. The resource profile makes this instance suitable for production relational databases, distributed caching layers, enterprise ETL pipelines, and high-concurrency static web serving.

It includes 512 GB of DDR4 memory at 3 GHz, offering an 8 GB per vCPU ratio, alongside 3800 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage and 25 Gbps baseline network throughput. The instance incorporates AVX-512, VAES, and hardware memory encryption. In benchmark testing, the server demonstrates strong results in PassMark database operations, PassMark CPU tests, and clang software compilation, alongside steady multi-core execution in stress-ng and Geekbench. While lacking discrete GPU hardware, its integrated NVMe storage and substantial RAM minimize input-output latency for memory-bound applications. The r6id.16xlarge is suited for enterprise in-memory caches, large database management systems, data processing pipelines, and high-throughput web serving.
